summary: Kitsap County, WA: summit lookout built 1947-48 (sources disagree on tower); a 1965 DNR tower was destroyed in 1972; footings remain; summit road crosses the restricted Bremerton Watershed.

facts.design: Original steel tower with 7x7 ft cab and ground house (sources give 75 or 85 ft); 1965 replacement was a 50-ft wooden DNR live-in tower on the next knob west
facts.status_note: Original tower torn down before 1974; 1965 tower destroyed in 1972; footings and survey benchmarks remain, per a 2023 visit reported by WillhiteWeb

staffing.status: last recorded staffing 1966 (Gloria and Dick Tyler)

access.note: The summit road passes through the restricted Bremerton Watershed; signs have disappeared and been reposted (per WillhiteWeb); public visit not settled in the sources read

events.note: Road cleared in 1947; a metal tower went up in 1948 with a 14x18 ft ground house. firelookout.com and the register date the first lookout to 1947.
Mary Lou (Baertschiger) Nelson, with help from Helen Walsh, in summer
DNR began the application process for 10 acres just west of the original site for a new live-in lookout
50-foot wooden DNR live-in tower built at a new location on the next knob west of the summit; the register and Forest Lookouts date it 1964-66
Gloria and Dick Tyler staffed the 1965 tower in 1965 and 1966; last staffing in the sources read
The 1965 tower was destroyed; WillhiteWeb says it is unclear why after only seven years
USGS survey party found the original tower already torn down with four leg bases remaining; the date of teardown is not given
Registered January 11, 2012 as US 1181, WA 82; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register and firelookout.com say first lookout built 1947 as an 85-foot steel tower. Forest Lookouts and WillhiteWeb put the metal tower in 1948 (road in 1947). The Division of Forestry annual report, as quoted by both sites, says 75-foot steel Navy surplus; the Kresek Inventory, as quoted by WillhiteWeb, says 85-foot MC-39 Aermotor iron; a 1954 USGS party described a wooden tower about 90 feet tall, and WillhiteWeb notes this contradicts steel but finds wood framing on the footings. The story reports the disagreement and uses 1948 as the year of the tower.

notes_for_editor: Brief record checked: status gone, 2012 registration, agency and elevation correct. The brief had no 'built' event; 1948 tower added with the 1947 date noted. Build date and tower type conflict across sources and the annual report was checked only second-hand through two sites, not against the primary report. Staffing and most history come from one hobby site (WillhiteWeb), with 2023 site observations. Do not confuse with the Gold Mountain in Ferry County (NHLR US 1526, standing) or the Gold Mountain in Stevens County. Access: the summit road crosses the restricted Bremerton Watershed; the story gives no route. Budget: 1 WebSearch, 5 page reads.
